mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 12 months of similar rate conditions (Granger causality rejected).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with the labor strength signal (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% suggests accelerating demand growth, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports S&P 500 positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 100 observations where the signal is positive but 20-day returns are negative (cumulative failure proportion > 30%).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer goods orders (not available in this catalog) would typically signal supply-side weakness, but here we proxy with INDPRO falling by > 5% in two consecutive months, predicting negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: More than 40% of triggered negative signals fail to predict negative returns (misleading false negatives).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%, it indicates a shift toward accommodative policy, which historically precedes a 5-day rally in the S&P 500, suggesting positive 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In 20% of such events, the 5-day forward return does not exceed the 1-day return (no acceleration).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (not directly observable; using PAYEMS as proxy) and stable unemployment (UNRATE) indicate tight labor markets, which can drive equity risk-on flows and produce positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases month-over-month while UNRATE remains flat or declines
failure_condition: No significant correlation between the labor signal and 20-day forward returns (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) below 2% suggests deflationary pressure, which often precedes equity market volatility and can result in negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% in a single month
failure_condition: More than 50% of such signals fail to precede negative 60-day returns (delayed or absent effect).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls by more than 0.3 percentage points in a single month while FEDFUNDS remains below 4%, it indicates a labor market strengthening without aggressive monetary tightening, which typically precedes a 20-day S&P 500 forward return gain.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by > 0.3pp and FEDFUNDS < 4% in the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is non-positive in over 70% of such triggered events (failure to materialize).
